title: AI job cull not for forward thinkers
full_text:
Companies laying off thousands of staff and replacing them with artificial intelligence are battling a “crisis of imagination”, according to human resources software behemoth Workday.
Workday senior vice-president of product Max Wessel – who likens companies to taking a Star Trek or Star Wars approach to management – says while AI will flatten middle management, it did not have to correlate with mass job losses.
“Right now, as an industry, we have a crisis of imagination. That’s why you see a lot of that focus on ‘hey, let’s use agents to automate white collar work’,” Mr Wessel said.
WiseTech Global billionaire Richard White has been one of the biggest advocates of so-called agentic AI – which can act semi or fully autonomously – saying an agent can be built within hours and do the job as good as a human. Those comments came as WiseTech sacked 2500.
WiseTech is not alone. Atlassian has laid off 1600, Amazon axed 16,000, while Uber has cut 3300 – or about 10 per cent of its workforce – among other widespread redundancies.
Mr Wessel – who spent eight years on the faculty of the Stanford Graduate School of Business, teaching and writing on strategy and product development – said AI foundation model companies and others who were more forward-thinking with the technology were “not reducing headcount”. He said they were “figuring out how to deploy people on bigger and bigger, more ambitious problems”.
“This crisis of imagination is I either take the first order decision and I say ‘I’m going to reduce my workforce’, and then end up having to hire later into a role where I actually might have good talent that can be redeployed, or I can look at the problem holistically.
“I can have my system scan my environment, understand every human, migrate them forward. In order to help guide folks through this process. We need to give them the tools that kind of inspire that imagination and make the risk of taking that might be the right decision into something that is easier managed.” Workday is providing the AI-powered tools that are automating much of the tasks assigned to middle management. Mr Wessell said this will change the “corporate ladder” but shouldn’t lead to retrenchment.
Mr Wessel agrees with former Atlassian futurist Dominic Price and Fortescue AI and IT director Ellie Coates that companies need to “redesign” the way they work rather than “bolt AI” onto existing corporate structures. And this is where he draws parallels with Star Trek and Star Wars. “There’s the Star Wars version of the world and the Star Trek version. We actually have some control over what happens. I don’t believe in a world where we are going to be scavengers on rim planets. We can actually become explorers. We can elevate humanity. We can give them (staff) higher purpose. But it requires that focus.”
